ud3.9:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Wood, at Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
ud3.9:1.3: Then at that time, amongst many monks, after returning from the alms-round after the meal, assembling together, and sitting in the Round Hall, this conversation arose:
ud3.9:1.4: “Now who, venerable friends, knows a craft?
ud3.9:1.5: Who has trained in what craft?
ud3.9:1.6: Which craft is the greatest of the crafts?”
ud3.9:2.2: Then some said this: “Elephant-craft is the greatest of the crafts,”
ud3.9:2.4: some said this: “Horse-craft is the greatest of the crafts,”
ud3.9:2.6: some said this: “Chariot-craft is the greatest of the crafts,”
ud3.9:2.8: some said this: “Bow-craft is the greatest of the crafts,”
ud3.9:2.10: some said this: “Sword-craft is the greatest of the crafts,”
ud3.9:2.12: some said this: “Finger-calculation-craft is the greatest of the crafts,”
ud3.9:2.14: some said this: “Abacus-craft is the greatest of the crafts,”
ud3.9:2.16: some said this: “Accountancy-craft is the greatest of the crafts,”
ud3.9:2.18: some said this: “Writing-craft is the greatest of the crafts,”
ud3.9:2.20: some said this: “Poetry-craft is the greatest of the crafts,”
ud3.9:2.22: some said this: “Natural philosophy-craft is the greatest of the crafts,”
ud3.9:2.24: some said this: “Political science-craft is the greatest of the crafts.”
ud3.9:2.25: Now this conversation that arose amongst those monks was left unfinished.
ud3.9:3.1: Then the Fortunate One, having risen from seclusion in the evening time, went to the Round Hall, and after going, he sat down on the prepared seat.
ud3.9:3.2: Having sat down the Fortunate One addressed the monks, (saying):
ud3.9:3.3: “What is the talk about, monks, amongst those who have assembled at present, and what is the conversation amongst you that was left unfinished?”
ud3.9:4.1: “Here, reverend Sir, after returning from the alms-round after the meal, assembling together, and sitting in the Round Hall, this conversation arose:
ud3.9:4.2: “Now who, venerable friends, knows a craft?
ud3.9:4.3: Who has trained in what craft?
ud3.9:4.4: Which of the crafts is the greatest of the crafts?”
ud3.9:5.2: Then some said this: “Elephant-craft is the greatest of the crafts,”
ud3.9:5.4: some said this: “Horse-craft is the greatest of the crafts,”
ud3.9:5.6: some said this: “Chariot-craft is the greatest of the crafts,”
ud3.9:5.8: some said this: “Bow-craft is the greatest of the crafts,”
ud3.9:5.10: some said this: “Sword-craft is the greatest of the crafts,”
ud3.9:5.12: some said this: “Finger-calculation-craft is the greatest of the crafts,”
ud3.9:5.14: some said this: “Abacus-craft is the greatest of the crafts,”
ud3.9:5.16: some said this: “Accountancy-craft is the greatest of the crafts,”
ud3.9:5.18: some said this: “Writing-craft is the greatest of the crafts,”
ud3.9:5.20: some said this: “Poetry-craft is the greatest of the crafts,”
ud3.9:5.22: some said this: “Natural philosophy-craft is the greatest of the crafts,”
ud3.9:5.24: some said this: “Political science-craft is the greatest of the crafts.”
ud3.9:5.25: This is the conversation, reverend Sir, that we left unfinished, then the Fortunate One arrived.”
ud3.9:6.1: “This is certainly not suitable, monks, for you sons of good family who through faith have gone forth from the home to homelessness, that you should talk such talk.
ud3.9:6.2: When you have assembled together, monks, there are two things that you ought to do:
ud3.9:6.3: talk about the Dhamma, or maintain noble silence.”
ud3.9:7.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
ud3.9:8.1: “One who lives without craft, light, desiring (others') welfare,
ud3.9:8.2: With restrained faculties, completely free in every way,
ud3.9:8.3: Who wanders homeless, unselfish, not yearning,
ud3.9:8.4: Having given up conceit, solitary - he is a monk.”
